For RGAA test 10.7.1. Evidence only. Runs in the keyboard pass, in a browser whose viewport size, device scale factor and colour scheme are recorded, with the pointer outside the viewport. Calibration: in the same browser context, a reference page holding one <button> with default styles; focus it with Tab and take a viewport screenshot, then blur it and take another; they must differ, otherwise answer error for the page (focus indicators are not being painted in this setup). Elements: each element of the top document, shadow trees included, that receives focus while Tab moves through the sequential focus order. For each, in this order: (1) after the key press the deep active element must be this element, otherwise cannot_tell for it. (2) If it is an iframe, frame, object, embed, video or audio element, cannot_tell. (3) If its border box is not entirely inside the viewport after the browser's own focus scrolling, or is under 4 CSS px wide or high, or it or an ancestor has computed opacity 0 or visibility hidden, or a clip or clip-path leaves less than 4 CSS px of it in either dimension, or an ancestor clips its overflow (overflow other than visible, clip-path, or contain including paint) within 4 CSS px of its border box, or an element that is neither it, its ancestor nor its descendant has a box intersecting its border box and is painted above it (pointer-events none included), cannot_tell (a native focus ring may be clipped or covered there without the style having been removed, and the wording does not settle whether that counts as degraded). (4) Wait until document.getAnimations() lists no running or pending animation or transition; if any remains after 1 s, cannot_tell. Take screenshot A of the viewport. (5) Start a MutationObserver on the document and every shadow root (attributes, child lists, character data, subtrees). Call blur() on the element and wait the same way, with the same cannot_tell after 1 s. (6) Read the deep active element (through shadow roots and frames): if it is the element, or the element still matches :focus, or focus is on any element other than the body, cannot_tell. If the scroll position changed, or the observer recorded any mutation, cannot_tell. Take screenshot B. (7) Fault when A and B are identical pixel for pixel. Otherwise no fault for the element; a difference is not taken to mean the indication is sufficient or contrasted. The fault is evidence only: the guards above make it likely that focusing the element changed nothing visible, but they do not prove it. A script can react to focus or blur without mutating the DOM (a timer that reapplies a style through the CSSOM, a canvas redrawn on focus), and an indication added when the element took focus and kept after blur is visible in both screenshots although the element did show focus. Elements that take focus only from a pointer or a script are not examined. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any element is cannot_tell or the pass did not complete; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element receives focus.

For RGAA test 11.1.1. Elements, in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included (if a nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page): form fields as the glossary lists them, that is <input> with no type attribute or of type text, password, search, email, number, tel, url, checkbox, radio, date, range, color, time, month, week, datetime-local or file; <textarea>; <select>; <output>; <progress>; <meter>; and elements with an explicit role of progressbar, slider, spinbutton, textbox, listbox, searchbox or combobox. Skipped as not fields (glossary): <input> of type submit, reset, hidden, image or button, <button>, and role="button". cannot_tell, never fault, for: <input> of any other type; <option>, <optgroup> and <datalist>; explicit roles option, checkbox, radio and switch (they may take a name from content, which no route of the test names); a role=combobox element that contains an <input>; a role=listbox element referenced by aria-controls or aria-owns of a combobox. For each remaining field, in this order: (1) not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse), or it or an ancestor has aria-hidden="true" or is inert: cannot_tell. (2) It has no aria-labelledby attribute, no aria-label attribute, no title attribute, an empty labels list (no <label> whose for equals its id in its tree, and no <label> ancestor that labels it), and no <label> ancestor at all: fault. Every condition of the test needs one of these, so the field meets none. (3) Otherwise cannot_tell: the check does not decide whether a present mechanism is sufficient (empty values, references to missing ids, a label without for, the adjacent-button condition). Page result: fault if any field has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if there is any field; inapplicable when there is none.

For RGAA test 11.1.2. Evidence only. Elements: every <label> element with a for attribute, in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. Fault on a label when its for value is empty, or when no element in the same tree (the document, or the shadow root holding the label) has an id equal to its for value: the label is tied to no element by for and id. The fault does not say which field the label was meant for, or that it was meant for a field at all. Page result: fault if any label has a fault; otherwise no_fault if at least one label has a for attribute; inapplicable when none has.

For RGAA test 2.1.1. Elements: every <iframe> and <frame> element in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. If any nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each frame element, in this order: (1) it has a title attribute whose value contains a non-whitespace character: the requirement holds for it. (2) It has a title attribute that is empty or only whitespace: cannot_tell (the wording asks for the attribute; the glossary defines the frame title as its content). (3) It has no title attribute and aria-hidden="true" is set on it, on an ancestor in its document, or on a frame element that hosts that document: cannot_tell, since the exception for technical frames hidden with aria-hidden may apply and deciding it needs judgment. (4) It has no title attribute and is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame that is itself not rendered), or is not exposed in the accessibility tree for another reason (inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element included): cannot_tell, since only aria-hidden carries an exception in the official text and no text says whether other hidden frames count. (5) Otherwise: fault on that element. The check ignores aria-label, aria-labelledby and role, which the test does not accept in place of title. Page result: fault if any frame falls under (5); otherwise cannot_tell if any falls under (2), (3) or (4); otherwise no_fault if there is at least one frame; inapplicable if there is no frame element at all.

For RGAA test 2.2.1, the empty-title case only; whether a non-empty title is relevant is not examined. Elements: every <iframe> and <frame> element that has a title attribute, in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. Frame elements without a title attribute are outside this test and are not examined. For each element, in this order: (1) An aria-hidden attribute with any value other than false (ignoring ASCII case and surrounding whitespace) is set on it, on an ancestor in its document, or on a frame element that hosts that document: cannot_tell, since the glossary's exception for technical frames hidden with aria-hidden may apply and whether a frame is technical needs judgment. (2) It is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame element that is itself not rendered), or it is not exposed in the accessibility tree for another reason (inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element included): cannot_tell, since the text of this test gives no exception for such frames and does not say whether they count. (3) Its title value is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020): fault on that element. An empty title tells nothing about the frame's content and is not a generic mention, and the frame is not hidden with aria-hidden, so no route and no exception holds. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: whether a non-empty title is relevant, or a fitting generic mention for a technical frame, is judgment. This includes a value made only of other invisible characters, such as no-break or zero-width spaces. Page result: fault if any element falls under (3); otherwise cannot_tell if any element falls under (1), (2) or (4), or if a nested document cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable, since no frame element has a title attribute. Never no_fault.

For RGAA test 6.2.1. Elements: in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every HTML element with an href attribute, every SVG element with an href or xlink:href attribute, and every element with an explicit role="link". An without href or xlink:href is an anchor and is skipped (technical note of criterion 6.2). If a nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each element, compute its name from content only, ignoring aria-labelledby, aria-label, title and xlink:title on the element itself: walk its descendants, skip every subtree that is hidden from assistive technologies (aria-hidden="true", computed display none, computed visibility hidden or collapse, the hidden attribute), and collect: the data of text nodes; for an or an element with role img or image, its text alternative from aria-labelledby, then aria-label, then alt, then title; for an inline

For RGAA test 7.3.2. Evidence only. Runs in the keyboard pass. Elements: every element that receives focus while the Tab key moves through the page's sequential focus order, in the top document, shadow trees included, and in nested frame documents that can be read. For each one: record the deep active element (through shadow roots and readable frames) right after the key press; then wait 500 ms with no input and read it again. Fault on the element when focus is now on the document body or on no element, while the element is still connected, rendered, not disabled, not inert and still focusable: its focus was removed without user action. cannot_tell for the element when focus has moved to another element or into a frame, or when the element was removed, hidden, disabled or made inert meanwhile (whether these count as removing focus is not decided here). Elements that can take focus only from a pointer are not examined, and the particular case of criterion 7.3 is not examined. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any element is cannot_tell or the pass did not complete; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element receives focus.

For RGAA test 7.3.1. Evidence only. Elements: in the top document, shadow trees included, every element with an event listener attached directly to it for click, dblclick, mousedown, mouseup, pointerdown, pointerup, touchstart, touchend, keydown, keyup or keypress, read through the DevTools protocol (DOMDebugger.getEventListeners, which includes on* attributes). Fault on such an element when it is rendered, not disabled, not inert, not in the sequential focus order (not natively focusable and without tabindex, or with a negative tabindex), and has no ancestor that is in the sequential focus order. cannot_tell for such an element when an ancestor is in the sequential focus order (keyboard activation of the ancestor may perform the same action). Listeners attached to window, document, html or body cannot be attributed to elements: when any of the event types above is listened for there, the page result is cannot_tell unless a fault exists. A fault says only that Tab cannot reach the element; it says nothing about an equivalent element elsewhere in the page, keyboard shortcuts, pointer access, or the particular case of criterion 7.3. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell as above; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element has such a listener.

For RGAA test 8.3.1. Scope: the top-level document of the page; documents in frames are read only for step 1. Document type: XHTML 1.1 when the doctype public identifier contains "XHTML 1.1"; XHTML 1.0 when it contains "XHTML 1.0", split by the served content type (document.contentType) into text/html and application/xhtml+xml; other XML when it contains "XHTML" otherwise or the document is served as application/xhtml+xml without one of those doctypes; otherwise HTML. Indication required on an element: HTML: lang; XHTML 1.0 as text/html: lang and xml:lang; XHTML 1.0 as application/xhtml+xml: xml:lang; XHTML 1.1: xml:lang; other XML: lang and xml:lang. xml:lang is read with getAttributeNS("http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace", "lang") in XML documents and as the attribute named xml:lang in text/html documents. An element carries the indication when every required attribute is present with a value holding a non-whitespace character. The check answers no_fault only through the html element. It never concludes that every text element carries the indication: the wording "chaque élément de texte" does not say which texts count (a field's value, text generated by CSS, alternative and title attributes, the page title, the text of framed documents), so no list of text items can be shown complete. Witness: a text node that is a text element under any reading of the wording, so that a fault never rests on text that could be decorative, hidden, invisible or a pictogram. A text node is a witness only when all of the following hold; a node that fails any of them is never a witness, whatever it holds. (a) Place: it is in the top-level document's tree, not in a shadow tree, inside body; body is an HTML element, and every element strictly between body and the node is an HTML element from this list: div, main, article, section, header, footer, nav, aside, address, center, p, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, dl, dt, dd, blockquote, figure, figcaption, table, caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, span, em, strong, b, i, u, s, small, big, mark, abbr, cite, q, dfn, time, data, sub, sup, ins, del, bdi, font; and neither body nor any of those elements is a shadow host or carries a role, aria-hidden, hidden or inert attribute, in any form or with any value. (b) Letters: its data holds two characters of Unicode general category L in a row, with only characters of category M between them. (c) Exposure: Chromium's full accessibility tree holds a node for it (static text whose backend DOM node is this text node) that is not ignored. (d) Font: every family in the computed font-family of its parent element is either one of the unquoted generic families serif, sans-serif, monospace, system-ui, ui-serif, ui-sans-serif and ui-monospace, or, quotes removed and ignoring ASCII case, a family on the pinned list of text fonts: Arial, Helvetica, Helvetica Neue, Times, Times New Roman, Georgia, Verdana, Tahoma, Trebuchet MS, Courier, Courier New, Lucida Grande, Lucida Sans Unicode, Segoe UI, Calibri, Cambria, Garamond, Palatino, Palatino Linotype, Book Antiqua, Geneva, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, Noto Sans, Noto Serif, DejaVu Sans, DejaVu Serif, Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif, Ubuntu, Cantarell (record the list's version with the check; it holds only fonts whose letter glyphs are letters, never an icon or symbol font); and document.fonts holds no FontFace whose family matches, ignoring ASCII case, any family in that computed font-family. This rules out icon fonts, whether they draw a pictogram from a word by ligature or from a single letter, symbol fonts such as Wingdings or Webdings, and any family the page defines itself. (e) Paint: the parent element and every ancestor element have computed opacity 1, filter none, mix-blend-mode normal, clip-path none, mask-image none and clip auto; the parent element has computed visibility visible, -webkit-text-security none, a font-size of at least 8 CSS pixels, and a color and -webkit-text-fill-color with alpha 1. (f) Contrast: walk from the parent element up its ancestors to the first whose computed background-color has alpha 1; no element on that walk, that one included, has a background-image other than none or a background-color with alpha strictly between 0 and 1. If no element up to html has an opaque background-color, the background is white, but only when the html element's computed color-scheme is normal; otherwise the node is not a witness. If the parent's computed -webkit-text-fill-color differs from its computed color, the node is not a witness, since the painted fill is what counts and the color alone would misstate the contrast; otherwise the contrast ratio (WCAG 2 formula) between the parent's color, which is then the painted fill, and that background is at least 2. (g) Geometry: take the rectangles Range.getClientRects() returns for the node; clip each to the padding box of every ancestor element whose computed overflow-x or overflow-y is not visible or whose computed contain includes paint, content or strict (whether or not that ancestor is its containing block), and to the viewport as loaded, without scrolling. At least one clipped rectangle is at least 4 CSS pixels wide and 4 high, and at its centre document.elementFromPoint returns the node's parent element itself (not a child, an ancestor or any other element painted above the text). No element other than the parent and its ancestors whose computed pointer-events is none has a border box containing that centre, since hit testing skips such an element although it may paint over the text. The parent element generates no ::before or ::after box (computed content none or normal for both), since hit testing reports a pseudo-element as its element. Uncovered witness: a witness with no lang or xml:lang attribute in any form, even empty, on any ancestor element. Answer, in this order: (1) The html element of the top-level document carries the indication its document type requires: no_fault, unless the page holds a rendered iframe or frame (with a layout box, in the top-level document or in a document nested through frames, shadow trees included) whose document cannot be read, or whose document holds a rendered or exposed text node with a non-whitespace character while its html element does not carry the indication its own document type requires; then cannot_tell (the wording does not say whether a framed document counts as part of the page for this test). (2) The html element has a lang or xml:lang attribute in any form (empty, whitespace only, or not the one its document type requires): cannot_tell. (3) The html element has neither a lang nor an xml:lang attribute in any form, and the page holds at least one uncovered witness: fault, reported on the first in tree order. That node is visible and exposed text in ordinary content, with no language indication on any parent, so the second route fails for it whichever texts are counted, and the first route fails because html has neither attribute. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: the html element has neither attribute and no witness is uncovered. Either the second route may hold, but the check cannot show that every text element is covered; or the only text without a language source is not a witness: hidden from assistive technologies or not exposed, invisible though laid out (opacity below 1, transparent or low-contrast colour, clipped, off-screen, covered, too small), drawn in an icon, symbol or page-defined font, a single letter, inside a link, control, label, code, ruby, SVG, MathML, shadow tree or an element with a role, outside body, in an attribute, a field's value, generated by CSS, or in a framed document. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.4.1, the validity condition only (relevance is not examined). Scope: the html element of the top-level document, with the document types, required attributes and way of reading xml:lang defined for custom/8-3-default-lang-present. For each required attribute present on the html element: if its value is empty or has leading or trailing whitespace, cannot_tell for it. Otherwise take the part of the value before the first hyphen (the whole value if there is none) and compare it, ignoring ASCII case, with a pinned list holding every ISO 639-1 code, every ISO 639-2 code in both its bibliographic and terminologic forms (including the reserved range qaa to qtz and the codes mis, mul, und and zxx), every ISO 639-3 code and every ISO 639-5 code, plus codes since deprecated or withdrawn from any of those parts (such as iw, in, ji, mo); record the list's version with the check. Fault on the attribute when that part is not in the list. When the html element has none of the required attributes, answer cannot_tell: the default language may be given on each text element instead, which this check does not examine, or be missing, in which case this test does not apply. Attributes on html that the document type does not require are not examined. Page result: fault if any required attribute has a fault; no_fault when every required attribute is present and its code is in the list; otherwise cannot_tell. Never inapplicable.
